main_body: Goblet-shaped stone font: an elliptical bowl of holy water on a stem and a flared base
top_band: Light grey-white rim ellipse at rows 2-3 around blue water at rows 3-7; the front lip is a light-grey band at about row 7-8
evidence: In the centre column I read a light rim at the top, then a blue water ellipse about 4 rows tall, then a light front lip. Below that is the grey bowl underside, a narrow stem and a flared base with a lighter top band. The opening reads as a real ellipse seen from above, like the green column and barrel guides, not a flat cap line. The foot also shows a small top plane. The foreshortened rim and water together take about 6 rows and sit above about 7 rows of front body and stem, so it counts as 3/4. There are no doors or drawers, so recessed_front is false.

style.evidence: The grey stone has about 3-4 tones and the water 3 blues, which is thinner than the 5-6 step ramps on the references. Outline is a neutral dark grey-blue with little tint, so it is mixed rather than a clear dark material tone. The stem, base and bowl body are smooth gradients with no grain, speckle or per-stone shading. Tiles carry only about 3-5 colours, well below the reference stall and well, which have tile scallops, wood grain and stone-by-stone shading. Next to them it looks thinner and more sticker-like.
